title: The effectiveness of various preventive measures on quality of life within the statutory health insurance system.
summary: AOK Baden-Württemberg offers its policyholders courses and advice on exercise, nutrition and relaxation. There are often several programmes with the same aim, for example various weight-loss courses. So far, little is known about which of these programmes is most beneficial to health. In this study, participants complete a short online questionnaire about their quality of life: at the start of the course, immediately after the course ends, and one year after the course began. This data is used to calculate how quality of life changes over the course of a year, and programmes with the same aim are compared with one another. The courses themselves will not be altered as a result of the study. Participation is voluntary, anonymous and takes around 5 to 10 minutes per survey. An email address may be provided to receive an invitation to the one-year follow-up survey; this will be stored separately from the responses and cannot be used to identify the participant. The results are intended to help in the targeted expansion of effective programmes.
conditions: Prevention of lifestyle-related diseases; health-related quality of life.

interventions.name: Course categories (exercise, nutrition, relaxation): Adult policyholders of AOK Baden-Württemberg, with or without pre-existing lifestyle-related conditions, who take part in a course intervention as part of standard practice at course venues in all regional offices. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
People insured with AOK Baden-Württemberg; participation in a covered prevention programme in the areas of physical activity, nutrition or relaxation; sufficient knowledge of German; electronic informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
No consent; no T0 questionnaire completed prior to the start of the intervention.
